PRINCIPLE.Definition: the basic idea of how something works

CHANGE.Definition: the money given back when you pay more than the price

SELLING POINT.Definition: a feature that makes something attractive to buyers or users

CONSTRAINTS.Definition: limits that stop someone doing more

PROFITABLE.Definition: making more money than is spent

COMMISSION.Definition: a part of the money from each sale, paid to the company that arranged it

GLUTEN-FREE.Definition: made without the protein found in wheat and similar grains, which some people cannot eat

MARGINS.Definition: amounts of profit left from each sale after costs are paid

SUSTAINABLE.Definition: able to continue for a long time

COMMISSIONS.Definition: parts of the money from sales, paid to the company that arranged them

DINE-IN.Definition: eating at the restaurant rather than at home

RELIANT.Definition: dependent; needing something in order to continue

INCENTIVES.Definition: things that encourage people to do something

BUSINESS MODEL.Definition: a company's plan for how it will make money

RACE TO THE BOTTOM.Definition: a situation where competitors keep cutting prices to win, which harms everyone

MODEL.Definition: a way of doing business and making money

FIXED COSTS.Definition: costs, such as rent, that stay the same however much is sold

TRAILER.Definition: a large box on wheels, pulled by a vehicle, used here as a kitchen

THANKLESS.Definition: hard and not appreciated by others

UNPREDICTABLE.Definition: changing a lot, so you cannot know in advance how much it will be

MINIMUM WAGE.Definition: the lowest pay per hour that employers are legally allowed to pay

SICK PAY.Definition: money paid to a worker who is too ill to work
